slides.title: Optional extension
slides.html:
Optional review repeat of 4.10 Day 2: the other two SSS cases.

Read the worked steps
StepReason
Case 2: CG meets line AB outside segment AB.Same setup as the 4.10 proof.
Subtract the equal base angles instead of adding them. You still get angle ACB = angle AGB.Theorem 9, then angle subtraction.
Case 3: CG passes through A or B, so A, C, G (or B, C, G) are on one line.Only one isosceles triangle remains.
That one isosceles triangle gives angle ACB = angle AGB directly.Theorem 9.
In every case, SAS finishes the proof.So SSS holds for all triangles.

slides.title: Review item 1
slides.html:
Triangle ABC ≅ triangle PQR. Which side matches CA?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

RP, because C matches R and A matches P.

Reveal second check

CA uses the third and first letters, and so does RP.

slides.title: Review item 2
slides.html:
Triangle ABC ≅ triangle DEF, BC = 2x + 3 and EF = 15. Find x.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

2x+3=15,2x=12,x=6.

Reveal second check

2(6)+3=15.

slides.title: Review item 3
slides.html:
AB = DE, AC = DF and angle A = angle D. Which test?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

SAS, because angle A is between sides AB and AC, and angle D is between sides DE and DF.

Reveal second check

these are the included angles.

slides.title: Review item 5
slides.html:
Two segments AD and BC cross at M, and M is the midpoint of both. Prove triangle AMB ≅ triangle DMC.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

AM=DM,BM=CM by midpoint; AMB=DMC by vertical angles; SAS.

Reveal second check

A↔D,M↔M,B↔C makes all three facts corresponding.

slides.title: Review item 7
slides.html:
AB = AC, angle B = (3x + 2) degrees and angle C = (5x - 16) degrees. Find x and the base angles.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

3x+2=5x-16 gives x=9 and both angles 29.

Reveal second check

27+2=45-16=29.

slides.title: Review item 8
slides.html:
In triangle ABC, angle B = angle C. Prove AB = AC.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Compare triangle ABC with triangle ACB. Angle B = angle C, angle C = angle B and BC = CB, so they are congruent by ASA. Then AB = AC by CPCTC.

Reveal second check

every fact used here was proved before SSS.

slides.title: Review item 9
slides.html:
Does matching all three angles (AAA) prove two triangles congruent?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

No. Side-2 and side-5 equilateral triangles have matching angles but unequal sides.

Reveal second check

A rigid motion keeps lengths, so it cannot turn a side of 2 into a side of 5.

slides.title: Review item 14
slides.html:
Circles of the same radius at A and B cross at P and Q. What must you define before you talk about M?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

M is the point where segment PQ crosses line AB. P and Q are on opposite sides of line AB, and both circles use the same radius, more than half of AB, so M is between A and B.

Reveal second check

A half-turn about the midpoint of AB exchanges P and Q, so the midpoint is also on PQ.

slides.title: Review item 16
slides.html:
Look at the figure. C1 and C2 are on the same ray from A, AB = 5, AC1 = 3 and AC2 = 5. C1 and C2 lie on the same circle centered at B. Explain why SSA fails here, without trig.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

The two triangles share angle A, because C1 and C2 are on the same ray from A. They share side AB. BC1 = BC2, because both are radii of the circle centered at B. But AC1 = 3 and AC2 = 5, so the triangles are not congruent.

Reveal second check

the two triangles do not have the same three side lengths.

slides.title: Common traps
slides.html: Keep vertex order matched. Establish congruence before CPCTC. AAA and SSA are not tests. SSS is proved here, not assumed. Define every point and check that circles cross twice.
